props.caption: Check summarizer input, not the session model's window.

props.title: Memory and compaction take separate paths
props.description: Run the compaction-model extension after pi-optmem so wake text stays out of the summary.

props.caption: Pi keeps its recent tail and uses the proposed fit guard before selecting a summarizer; OptMem supplies persistent memory separately.
props.code:
flowchart TD
  trigger["Pi reaches configured threshold"] --> prep["Prepare span, recent tail and prior summary"]
  prep --> clean["OptMem saves facts and removes old wake text"]
  clean --> estimate["Estimate input plus output budget"]
  estimate --> guard{"Fits Haiku with 1.2x margin?"}
  guard -->|Yes| haiku["Haiku with native prompt and short instructions"]
  guard -->|No| fallback["Session model with explained fallback"]
  haiku --> replace["Replace old span, retain recent tail"]
  fallback --> replace
  clean --> memory["Persistent memory store"]
  memory --> wake["Wake view on later request"]

props.title: Proposed fit policy
props.code:
estimatedInputTokens = serializedMessageCharacters / 4
                     + priorSummaryTokens
                     + approximately 1500 prompt tokens
outputBudget = min(floor(0.8 * reserveTokens), model.maxTokens)
too_large = estimatedInputTokens * 1.2 + outputBudget > model.contextWindow
props.caption: The estimator is a proposed safeguard, not a verified exact tokenizer.
File operations contribute path lists, not file contents; summary input truncates tool results to 2,000 characters.

props.text: Keep the saved prior summary fixed across arms. Original pass bar: Haiku scores at least 90% of baseline, and no category scores zero on three or more spans. Report results by baseline model and include summary length. Keep raw session spans local and out of git.

Do not build normal-context masking, file or todo re-injection, or a new handoff system. Keep Pi's iterative structured prompt. The review allows logging actual sizes first if the fit check grows. On a Claude CLI subscription, the practical gain is speed and usage-limit headroom, not dollar savings.
